item.title: Check Point 2026 AI Security Report, VoidLink, s1ngularity Nx and Shai-Hulud
item.content:encoded:
AI Security Report 2026 — Should Read

Check Point Research’s AI Security Report 2026 warns that AI has evolved from helping attackers prepare campaigns to actively operating live intrusions, building malware, scaling phishing/vishing, and enabling convincing identity fraud. The report also highlights growing enterprise risks from prompt injection and sensitive data leakage through GenAI tools.

  • Check Point Research’s Annual AI Security Report 2026 says AI has moved from being an assistant that helps attackers prepare to an operator that performs hands-on work inside live intrusions.
  • The report says AI has been used in live intrusions ranging from China-nexus espionage campaigns to a criminal breach of multiple Mexican government agencies.
  • The report says AI can build deployment-ready malware and attack suites, citing VoidLink, an 88,000-line command-and-control offensive framework produced in under a week using an AI environment.
  • The report says attackers often favor jailbroken mainstream commercial models and increasingly abuse agentic architecture through planted configuration files that agents load and trust across sessions.
  • The report says enterprise data leakage through GenAI is a persistent and growing risk, with high-risk prompts doubling from 2% to 4% during the last year.

How Aikido Intel detects malware and vulnerabilities first — Optional

Aikido Intel is a real-time supply-chain intelligence feed that monitors open-source package ecosystems to detect both malicious packages and undisclosed vulnerabilities within minutes. Its pipeline combines deobfuscation, static and sandbox analysis, AI review, and human researcher validation to reduce false positives and catch novel attacks quickly.

  • Aikido Intel is a real-time open feed that tracks both malware and undisclosed vulnerabilities across open-source ecosystems.
  • In the second quarter of 2026, Aikido Intel analyzed around 7.5 million package versions and confirmed 19,500 malicious packages.
  • Aikido Intel monitors new package releases, extracts and deobfuscates package contents, applies static rules and npm sandbox analysis, and uses AI plus human review for harder cases.
  • Aikido’s researchers were among the first to report major npm supply chain campaigns including the s1ngularity Nx attack and the Shai-Hulud worm.
  • Aikido recommends waiting a day or two before adopting brand-new package releases and using Aikido Safe Chain to block confirmed malware or npm packages less than 24 hours old.
